title: Rollback suggestion engine: opinionated simulation, confidence bands, and safe-apply workflow
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: We frequently ship config changes that tune batching/caching and autoscaler policies to reduce unit cost, but the downstream risk to tail latency and correctness can be non-linear. Current automatic reverts are binary and reactive: they wait for a threshold breach and then undo. We need a more nuanced system that: (1) simulates the expected impact before apply, (2) surfaces a rollback suggestion with confidence bands and cost/latency trade-offs, and (3) offers a safe-apply + staged auto-revert flow with state reconciliation to avoid flapping and partial state mismatch across fleets.

This ticket implements the "Rollback Suggestion Engine" (RSE): a service that runs opinionated dry-run simulations against historical traffic, produces a delta-score and confidence band, and integrates with the deploy pipeline to create an actionable suggestion (auto-approve, require manual approval, or block). It also wires a state-reconciliation walker to ensure the runtime and config store converge after any revert.

Goals:
- Produce deterministic simulated metrics for a proposed config change (latency p50/p95/p99, token-cost, throughput) using replay + stochastic perturbations (to model load variance).
- Emit a single "delta-score" (signed) and confidence band with recommended action: allow, staged-canary, require-approval, block.
- Provide a safe-apply mode: staged rollout with pre-configured guardrails and hysteresis to avoid flapping; if breached, trigger an automated suggestion to revert or partial rollback with a human-facing runbook.
- Ensure state reconciliation can repair partial rollbacks and reconcile KV caches and autoscaler state without manual intervention.

Non-goals:
- First pass does not change low-level kernel/runtime code or implement new batching algorithms. It only reasons about config changes and coordinates safe application and reversion flows.

Trade-offs considered:
- Heavyweight simulation vs. fast heuristics: we implement a two-tier approach: a fast heuristic delta-score for CI gating and an offline high-fidelity replay for release windows.
- Automatic revert aggression: use confidence bands + hysteresis windows to avoid oscillation (we prefer staged partial rollback over full immediate revert).
- Scope of reconciliation: start with in-memory KV cache and autoscaler state; defer persistent state reconciliation (e.g., custom plugin state) to follow-up tickets.
acceptance_criteria: RSE produces a delta-score and confidence band for any config change in the staging pipeline
Deploy pipeline receives suggestion and follows recommended action (allow/staged/require-approval/block) in 95% of synthetic tests
Safe-apply mode performs staged rollout with at least two verification gates (latency and error-rate) and honors hysteresis
Automatic suggestion to revert triggers only after sustained breach across hysteresis window and does not flip-flop during intermittent transient spikes
Reconciliation walker can detect partial rollback drift between config-store and runtime for KV cache headers and autoscaler desired-replicas and repair to last-known-good state in a canary subset
updates: 2026-03-03 — Aisha Kumar: Created initial spec and prototype design doc in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/RSE-spec. Chose two-tier simulation approach (fast delta + high-fidelity replay).

2026-03-06 — Riley Chen: Spike completed: replay harness runs against 7 days of sampled production traces and produces p50/p95/p99 deltas; baseline run time for a single config diff ~ 35s for fast-mode, ~9m for replay-mode. Patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1724
2026-03-09 — Infrastructure note (Miguel Santos): Provisioned r5-large ephemeral runners and a small S3 bucket for trace shards for replay. Added IAM role for RSE service account.
2026-03-10 — Riley Chen: Implemented delta-score aggregator and confidence estimator (bootstrap sampling). Unit tests added. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/deploy/pull/588

2026-03-12 — Design feedback (Jordan Patel): Suggested UI affordances for suggestions in Console: show cost delta, latency delta, confidence band, and clear next steps (Auto-approve/Manual/Block). Created Console PR reference: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/934

2026-03-13 — Safety review (SRE team): Agreed on hysteresis default = 10m sustained breach and staged rollout step size = 20% traffic shards. SRE requested metrics and alerting hooks for p99 latency regressions and rollback suggestion rate.
2026-03-14 — Current: In integration. End-to-end flow wired: pipeline -> RSE -> deployer. Need to finalize runbook text and add reconciliation repair operation to runtime agent.
comments: Riley Chen (2026-03-05): Observed that replay-mode can show different sign on delta for P99 compared to fast heuristics under bursty workloads — this is why we need confidence bands.

Aisha Kumar (2026-03-07): For cost-sensitive customers, we should expose an aggression knob (favor-cost vs favor-latency). Will add to config-schema as 'safety_profile' with values conservative|balanced|aggressive.
Miguel Santos (2026-03-11): Reminder: put limits on how many auto-reverts can execute per-day per-customer to avoid churn and noise — suggest metric 'auto_revert_count' with SLA rate cap.

Jordan Patel (2026-03-13): UX note: don't surface raw delta-score to end users; provide human-friendly guidance and an explainability panel showing top contributing signals (batch size change, cache TTL change, autoscaler thresholds).
